entries.claim: The edit treats a matching device/inode pair as proof that the destination was not replaced, but Unix inode numbers can be reused; the replacement test deliberately keeps the original directory alive and therefore cannot expose this bypass.
entries.failure_scenario: While confirmation waits, an attacker renames the checked directory away, removes it, and creates replacement directories on the same filesystem until the destination receives the original inode number. The replacement is empty, owner-owned, and 0700, so D-07 passes, and its device/inode pair matches the recorded pair, so the move proceeds despite AC4 requiring every replacement while the prompt waits to be refused. The proposed replacement test passes on this wrong implementation because retaining the renamed original directory prevents its inode from being reused.

counter_evidence.note: A replacement that reuses the inode must also pass the D-07 rule Task 2 applies: an empty 0700 directory owned by this uid. No other account can create one, so only this uid or root could stage the swap, which crosses no boundary. Low, not high.
